questions.prompt: After switching providers, a classifier starts returning 'The category is: Billing.' instead of 'BILLING'. What was the root cause?

options.text: The prompt relied on the old model's default behavior instead of an explicit format
Billing is not a valid category
The new model doesn't support classification

questions.explanation: Portable prompts state the format explicitly, show examples, and validate in code, so they don't depend on one model's habits.

questions.prompt: Which practices improve prompts that include images? Select all that apply.

options.text: Say exactly what to look at or extract
Label multiple images and refer to them by label
Ask for a description before the analysis
Trust all numbers read from the image without checking

questions.explanation: Focused instructions, labels, and describe-then-analyze help. Numbers read from images should be validated.

questions.prompt: Trying a cheaper model first and escalating to a stronger one when validation fails is called a model ____.
questions.explanation: Cascades pay for the expensive model only when needed, as long as you can detect failure.

questions.prompt: Which is the best way to decide which model to use for a task?

options.text: Pick the one with the best reputation online
Test candidates on your own test set, weighing quality, cost per completed task, latency, and data needs
Use whichever model a book describes as 'the creative one'

questions.explanation: Models change with every release. Choose with data from your own task rather than folklore.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of a safe prompt migration to a new model.

items.text: Simplify: remove workarounds the old model needed
Run your test set on old and new models with the current prompt
Re-run, compare, and only then switch traffic

questions.explanation: Measure first, learn what changed, simplify before adding, then verify before switching.

questions.prompt: Match each image-generation prompt ingredient to an example.

pairs.right: Wide shot with empty sky on the left
No text or logos in the image

questions.explanation: Image models respond to descriptive ingredients rather than instructions about the task.
